takeaways: The supported way into Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations is its REST/OData API, while direct SQL scripts, screen scraping and shadow integrations break with updates and create audit risk.

Every call needs a token from Azure AD (Entra ID): register the app, grant only the minimum API permissions, use the client credentials flow, and prefer certificates or managed identities over long-lived secrets.

Use OData for standard CRUD on entities and X++ custom services for multi-table, rule-driven logic, and protect both with least privilege, UAT testing, monitoring, throttling-aware retries and a runbook per integration.
hook: If integrating Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations has ever meant token errors, permission drama and fragile SQL scripts, this survival guide is for you. Admins and integration developers learn how Azure AD authentication, OData endpoints, custom services and dual-write fit together, plus the guardrails that keep ERP integrations supported and auditable.
